ledger.claim: The colleague works at a small nonprofit and is asking whether to use an AI service.
ledger.request_basis: a colleague at a small nonprofit who asks whether they should use an AI service

ledger.claim: The notes are confidential intake notes and the decision is needed for a meeting tomorrow.
ledger.request_basis: summarise confidential intake notes. They need a practical answer for a meeting tomorrow

sentences.text: You’re deciding whether a small nonprofit should use an AI service to summarise confidential intake notes before tomorrow’s meeting.
At first glance, it sounds like a straightforward way to save time—but confidentiality changes the answer.
The practical recommendation is: don’t put the notes into a general-purpose AI service unless the organization has first approved that specific service for confidential data.
A polished summary isn’t worth creating a new privacy, security, or mission risk (especially when the people described in the notes may have little power to object).
Ask the provider four questions: Will the service retain the notes, use them to improve its models, allow human review, or disclose them to other vendors?
If the answer to any of those questions is unclear, the service should not receive the notes.
The nonprofit should also confirm where the data is processed, how access is controlled, how deletion works, and whether the contract creates obligations the organization can actually meet.
Those details matter more than whether the model produces fluent prose.
Could you use AI at all? Possibly—but only with a workflow designed around data minimization.
Remove names and other identifying details, provide only the minimum context needed, and have a staff member check every summary against the original notes.
That is more like handing a volunteer a carefully redacted case file than handing a stranger the filing cabinet.
For tomorrow, bring a clear yes-or-no proposal: pause the integration unless the service passes the nonprofit’s privacy review and the team can explain the safeguards in plain language.
We can revisit the question after that review, but we should not make confidential intake notes the test case.
